<system-reminder>
Connector tools let you act on the user's connected external apps (for example GitHub, Linear, Jira) through the ConnectorSearch tool. When connectivity is known, connected tools are listed in a separate reminder, so no discovery call is needed for listed tools.

Connectors usage rules:
- An enabled MCP server or a skill dedicated to that same service takes priority; use connectors only when neither covers the need. A generic browser, scraping, or shell fallback does not count as covering a service.
- When a connected connector tool matches what the user needs from an external app, call it via ConnectorSearch (action "call_tool") instead of the shell or web search.
- The connectivity reminder lists only connected apps, so an app missing from it may still be offered by the organization and merely unconnected. Never conclude that no connector exists for an app without checking, and never tell the user an app is unavailable on that basis.
- For an app that is not listed as connected, and that the user needs data or actions from (including a link they pasted): use its MCP server tools if any; otherwise call ConnectorSearch "list_tools" (without authenticatedOnly) to check whether the organization offers it, then "call_tool". If the result asks for authentication, share the returned connect link with the user and retry after they connect. Fall back to a browser, scraping, or the shell only after that check shows the app is not offered.
- Refer to the brokering platform as "Connectors" or by the specific app's name (for example GitHub); share connect links as-is without drawing attention to the underlying provider.
- A connected app is not permission to act on the user's behalf. Reads are fine, and when the user asks for a write (posting a Slack or Teams message, sending an email, commenting, approving or landing a pull request, changing an issue), carry it out through the connector and send only what they asked for. Never write on your own initiative: for a write the user did not request, ask for explicit permission first and then send only what they approved.
</system-reminder>

Read the relevant section before that class of change. - `docs/test-lanes.md` owns named test lanes. Prefer the `pnpm run test:*` aliases over copying raw Vitest selectors. - `repository/topology.json` owns workspace boundaries and release bundles. - `package.json` owns the current command names. Inspect it instead of copying command details into new documentation. - Use the GitHub MCP server for GitHub operations. Use `gh` only when the GitHub MCP server cannot complete the operation because of a token problem. ## Runtime and package manager Use mise for Node.js and pnpm. The repository pins Node.js 24 and pnpm 12 in `mise.toml`; install the pinned tools before running development commands: ```bash mise install ``` Run Node.js and pnpm commands through mise so they do not fall back to system installations. Use `mise exec -- pnpm ...`, `mise exec -- npx ...`, and `mise exec -- node ...` in setup, validation, and troubleshooting commands. Git hooks are managed by hk. After `mise install`, enable them once per clone with: ```bash mise exec hk -- hk install --mise ``` ## Repository shape and boundaries The root is a private workspace orchestrator and has no runtime `src/` tree. The six workspaces are: - `packages/hevy-client` — runtime-neutral native-fetch Hevy client, curated exports, and Kubb-generated API types/schemas. - `packages/operations` — runtime-neutral reusable Hevy domain operations. - `packages/core` — runtime-neutral MCP server construction, tools, prompts, resources, execution, and safe diagnostics. - `packages/node` — public Node package `hevy-mcp`; Node lifecycle, stdio and local Streamable HTTP transports, telemetry, and Node built-ins. - `packages/worker` — private Cloudflare Worker Streamable HTTP and optional OAuth adapter. - `packages/cli` — public Node package `@chrisdoc/hevy-cli`; the standalone Hevy command-line client. The dependency direction is `hevy-client -> operations -> core`, with `core` also depending directly on `hevy-client`; Node, Worker, and CLI are adapters that consume the runtime-neutral packages. Adapters do not import one another. Keep Node built-ins and Cloudflare bindings out of `hevy-client`, `operations`, and `core`. Keep Node-only lifecycle, transport, telemetry, and observability in `packages/node`; keep Worker bindings and OAuth in `packages/worker`. ## Generated client Treat every file under `packages/hevy-client/src/generated/` as generated output. Change the OpenAPI source or the Kubb configuration, then regenerate: ```bash mise exec -- pnpm run openapi # refreshes the upstream spec; needs network access mise exec -- pnpm run build:client mise exec -- pnpm run check:openapi mise exec -- pnpm run check:generated ``` Review the complete generated diff. Consumers use the curated `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client`, `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client/types`, and `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client/schemas` exports; generated API functions and `.kubb` internals are private. Upstream schema corrections belong in `scripts/openapi-spec.js` so regeneration remains reproducible. ## MCP and type-safety conventions MCP tools live in `packages/core/src/tools/`. Follow the existing tool-definition pattern when adding or changing one: 1. Put the Zod input shape in the relevant tool file or `tools/input-schemas.ts`. 2. Derive handler arguments with `InferToolParams`; keep the schema as the single source of truth for validation and types. 3. Define the response contract and output schema for read tools in `utils/response-contracts.ts`. 4. Register the definition through `tools/register.ts`, use the existing `ToolRuntime` error/observation path, and add a co-located test. 5. Measure token cost when tool descriptions or schemas materially change: `pnpm run measure:tokens`. Handlers receive inferred arguments. Keep manual argument casts, `any`, and `unknown` out of tool-handler code. Reuse the existing error policy, `withErrorHandling` path, response contracts, and safe diagnostics rather than creating parallel response or error formats. ## Secrets and runtime behavior Use `HEVY_API_KEY` through `.env` or the process environment. Keep `.env` and real keys untracked, and keep keys out of command-line arguments, URLs, logs, fixtures, screenshots, and error messages. Deterministic unit, mocked MCP, contract, stdio, package, and performance lanes use fake credentials and do not need a live key. Live Hevy lanes require a valid `HEVY_API_KEY`. The Node executable defaults to stdio and also supports local Streamable HTTP with `--transport http`; inspect `packages/node/README.md` or `--help` before changing transport behavior. The Worker serves stateless Streamable HTTP at `POST /mcp`, authenticates the request bearer value, and keeps OAuth optional behind the `OAUTH_KV` binding. Read the Worker section of `CONTRIBUTING.md` before changing deployment, origin, authentication, or OAuth behavior. ## Changesets and release identity Before every commit, classify the diff and run: ```bash pnpm run check:changeset ``` A change under `packages/*`, a runtime-visible behavior change, a workspace dependency change, or `cloudflare.config.ts` requires a non-empty bump Changeset. Name the changed package and every transitive shipped consumer from `repository/topology.json`; do not couple unrelated packages. The current cascade is: - `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client` -> `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client`, `@hevy-mcp/operations`, `@hevy-mcp/core`, `hevy-mcp`, `@hevy-mcp/worker`, `@chrisdoc/hevy-cli`. - `@hevy-mcp/operations` -> `@hevy-mcp/operations`, `@hevy-mcp/core`, `hevy-mcp`, `@hevy-mcp/worker`, `@chrisdoc/hevy-cli`. - `@hevy-mcp/core` -> `@hevy-mcp/core`, `hevy-mcp`, `@hevy-mcp/worker`, `@chrisdoc/hevy-cli`. - Node-only, Worker-only, and CLI-only changes bump only their respective package; `cloudflare.config.ts` is a Worker change. Core, client, operations, and Worker are private but versioned for internal release/deployment identity. Node and CLI are public. Merge the automated `changeset-release/main` Version Packages pull request on the routine cadence (weekly by default); reserve off-cycle releases for security fixes and high-impact user-facing bugs. An entirely no-release, repository-only change may use an eligible empty Changeset via `npx changeset --empty`; docs, CI, repository-only tests/tooling, and chores qualify only when no release trigger is present. An empty Changeset never accompanies a release trigger. Stage the Changeset before committing. ## Validation workflow For source changes, run the narrow relevant lane and the unit suite. Before a pull request, use the repository baseline from `CONTRIBUTING.md`: ```bash mise exec -- pnpm run check mise exec -- pnpm run check:types mise exec -- pnpm run build mise exec -- pnpm run test:pr mise exec -- pnpm run test:performance mise exec -- pnpm run check:changeset ``` Useful focused checks include: - `pnpm run test:stdio` after MCP SDK, stdio, lifecycle, or Node transport changes. `packages/node/src/utils/stdio-observability.ts` uses private MCP SDK fields, so inspect compatibility after every SDK upgrade. - `pnpm run test:worker`, `pnpm run test:worker-http`, and `pnpm run worker:dry-run` after Worker changes. - `pnpm run test:pack` or `pnpm run test:pack:cli` after package entry point, binary, manifest, or published-file changes. - `pnpm run check:server-manifest` after server metadata changes. - `pnpm run check:boundaries` after workspace dependency or runtime-boundary changes. `pnpm run test:unit` is the deterministic default for local source work. `npm test` builds first and runs broad Vitest discovery; it is not a substitute for the named PR lanes. Integration, live, nightly, and live Worker commands are credential-gated and should be run only when the relevant safe credentials and environment are available. Known environment-dependent operations: - `pnpm run openapi` needs network access to the upstream Hevy API and may fail with `ENOTFOUND api.hevyapp.com` in a sandbox. - `pnpm run inspect` may time out without a correctly configured MCP client or browser environment. Treat all other documented checks, including `pnpm run check:types`, as real failures to investigate. ## Completion checklist Before reporting completion, confirm that the diff is focused, tests and checks for the changed paths passed (or their limitations are explicit), generated output is synchronized, the release requirement is satisfied, and `git status --short --branch` shows only intended files on the feature branch. This repo has the entire-graph code graph installed. Before exploring code with grep/find/whole-file reads, read .entire/graph-agent.md — resolution-first guidance for using graph retrieval, focused source inspection, and verification. @.entire/graph-agent.md # Ultracite Code Standards This project uses **Ultracite**, a zero-config preset that enforces strict code quality standards through automated formatting and linting. ## Quick Reference - **Format code**: `pnpm run fix` - **Check for issues**: `pnpm run check` - **Diagnose setup**: `pnpm exec ultracite doctor` Oxlint + Oxfmt (the underlying engine) provides robust linting and formatting. Most issues are automatically fixable. --- ## Core Principles Write code that is **accessible, performant, type-safe, and maintainable**. Focus on clarity and explicit intent over brevity. ### Type Safety & Explicitness - Use explicit types for function parameters and return values when they enhance clarity - Prefer `unknown` over `any` when the type is genuinely unknown - Use const assertions (`as const`) for immutable values and literal types - Leverage TypeScript's type narrowing instead of type assertions - Use meaningful variable names instead of magic numbers - extract constants with descriptive names ### Modern JavaScript/TypeScript - Use arrow functions for callbacks and short functions - Prefer `for...of` loops over `.forEach()` and indexed `for` loops - Use optional chaining (`?.`) and nullish coalescing (`??`) for safer property access - Prefer template literals over string concatenation - Use destructuring for object and array assignments - Use `const` by default, `let` only when reassignment is needed, never `var` ### Async & Promises - Always `await` promises in async functions - don't forget to use the return value - Use `async/await` syntax instead of promise chains for better readability - Handle errors appropriately in async code with try-catch blocks - Don't use async functions as Promise executors ### React & JSX - Use function components over class components - Call hooks at the top level only, never conditionally - Specify all dependencies in hook dependency arrays correctly - Use the `key` prop for elements in iterables (prefer unique IDs over array indices) - Nest children between opening and closing tags instead of passing as props - Don't define components inside other components - Use semantic HTML and ARIA attributes for accessibility: - Provide meaningful alt text for images - Use proper heading hierarchy - Add labels for form inputs - Include keyboard event handlers alongside mouse events - Use semantic elements (`

# entire-graph — instructions for coding agents (follow directly)

You have a deterministic local code graph: `entire graph` (functions, classes, methods,
types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the
agent reading this file. Use the graph to narrow exploration without trading away correctness.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.

## Hard rules

1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.
2. READ focused source around the result. Widen the check when aliases, generated code, dynamic
   dispatch, or related implementations could matter.
3. Use graph follow-ups only when they answer a real question. For impact or callers, prefer:
       entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X
4. Make the smallest complete edit and check sibling sites or contracts when the task implies them.
5. VERIFY before stopping. Run the most focused relevant test, build, or reproduction available.
   If execution is unavailable, perform a bounded source-level verification and state the limit.
6. Prefer precise queries and line ranges, but never trade resolution for fewer turns.
7. Feature-detect before relying on semantic relations:
       entire graph capabilities --json

## When NOT to use the graph

If the task already names the exact file and it is small, just read it — the graph saves tokens
by eliminating exploration; when there is nothing to explore, skip it.

# High-leverage Effect TS adoption

# High-Leverage Effect TS Adoption in hevy-mcp

## Plan Overview

This mission completes Effect adoption where it pays off: the Hevy request seam, a full Effect-first domain operations layer, core workflows/cache/resources, and the CLI consumer. Node stdio and Cloudflare Worker stay thin Promise adapters. Public MCP/CLI behavior stays the same; internals get typed errors, Stream pagination, DateTime windows, and Effect Cache.

At the end, workers open a GitHub PR from a feature branch based on `origin/main`. Live Hevy is out of scope. Validation is deterministic.

## Expected Functionality

### Milestone 1 — `client-seam`

Expand the internal Effect request client so operations can cover every Hevy resource without Promise hops.

- Extend `HevyRequestEffectClient` beyond the four reads (`getWorkouts`, `getWorkout`, `getRoutines`, `getRoutineById`) to templates, folders, body measurements, workout events, workout count, user info, and mutations.
- Keep the public `HevyClient` Promise API stable.
- Map HTTP failures onto existing `Schema.TaggedError` types (`NotFoundError`, `NetworkError`, `ValidationError`, `ApiError`, `RateLimitError`) instead of throwing generic defects.
- Preserve the single request-effect interpreter and retry schedule.

### Milestone 2 — `ops-foundation`

Make operations Effect-first and deepen the existing workouts/routines reads.

- Operations return `Effect` programs (`Effect.fn` + generator style). Thin Promise wrappers exist only where a current caller still needs them during the transition.
- Replace thrown page-mismatch defects with a typed `PaginationMismatchError`.
- Soft-404 / end-of-list handling uses tagged errors, not untyped `classifyReadError` heuristics.
- Update `effect-collapse.test.ts`: the single `runPromise` boundary moves to MCP/CLI/resource handlers, not `operation.execute`.
- Expand `HevyOperations` with a composable shape operations, core, and CLI can share.

### Milestone 3 — `ops-complete`

Complete the domain operations layer, including mutations and composite workflows.

Reads: templates, folders, body measurements, workout events, workout count, user info.

Writes: create/update workouts (including RMW replace-exercises), routines, templates, folders, body measurements. Mutation quirks currently in core (`mutation-semantics.ts`, timestamp normalize, `is_private`, rep ranges, omit-nulls) move into operations.

Composites: training-summary window scan and routine discovery pagination live in operations via `Stream.paginate` + `DateTime`, with bounded concurrency (`Effect.all`) instead of `while (true)` / `Promise.all` / raw `Date`.

### Milestone 4 — `core-runtime`

Wire core tools, resources, and cache through operations.

- All registered MCP tools use `HevyOperationsService` instead of ad-hoc `HevyClient` calls.
- Resources (`hevy://user`, `hevy://workout-count`, `hevy://exercise-templates`, `hevy://routine-folders`) share the same ops/cache path.
- Replace `AsyncTtlCache` with `Cache.make`. Construct the cache once in `createHevyMcpServer` (session/process scope), provide it through the request-local Layer. Do not allocate Cache per request, or Node will lose TTL hits across tool calls.
- Tool handlers collapse Effect to Promise **once** via `ToolRuntime.createHandler`.
- Keep MCP SDK / Node / Worker transports as Promise bridges.

### Milestone 5 — `cli-hygiene`

- Point remaining CLI commands at the new operations (user, workouts get/create/update/count/events, routines get/create/update, exercises, measurements, folders, summary).
- Do not export Effect types from public `hevy-mcp` or `@chrisdoc/hevy-cli`.
- Cascade Changeset for hevy-client → operations → core → hevy-mcp → worker → cli.
- Full `check` + `test:pr`.
- Open a GitHub PR against `main`.

## Architecture

Confirmed design:

```text
Public HevyClient (Promise, stable)
        │
        └─ NATIVE_REQUEST_EFFECT (internal)
                  │
                  ▼
         HevyRequestEffectClient  (all resources)
                  │
                  ▼
         HevyOperations  (Effect-first domain)
           reads | writes+quirks | composites (Stream + DateTime)
                  │
         ┌────────┼────────┐
         ▼        ▼        ▼
       core     CLI     (node/worker via core only)
    tools + resources
    Effect Cache (server-scoped)
         │
         ▼
    Promise collapse once
    (MCP handler / CLI command / resource reader)
```

**Boundaries**

- `hevy-client → operations → core`. Node and Worker must not import operations or `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client/internal`. CLI may import operations.
- Core must not import `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client/internal`.
- Effect Cache lives next to the catalog in `createHevyMcpServer`, then `Layer.succeed` into request-local DI.
- Public package exports stay Promise-shaped.

**Effect 4 RC.112 rules workers must follow**

- `Effect.fn("name")` + `Effect.gen`; never `const f = () => Effect.gen(...)`.
- Pagination: `Stream.paginate` (there is no `Stream.paginateEffect`).
- Cache: `Cache.make` / `Cache.makeWith`. No `cachedWithTTL`.
- Time: `DateTime.now` is an Effect value, not a function. Tests use `TestClock.layer()`.
- Errors: `Schema.TaggedError`; `return yield* new MyError(...)` inside generators.
- `Context.Service` (not `Context.Tag`). Import `Schema` from `effect`.

# Collapse operations Effect nesting and wire core layer

# Plan Overview

Collapse the nested `Effect.runPromise` in `@hevy-mcp/operations` so each of the four read operations is one Effect program with a single `runPromise` at the public Promise `execute()` boundary. Do that by consuming an **internal** Hevy client Effect seam (`requestEffect` on the native/Kubb client), not by changing the public Promise `HevyClient`. Then wire the unused `createCoreServiceLayer` into **all 22** registered MCP tools so 18 tools take `HevyClientService` and 4 take `HevyOperationsService`, without changing MCP JSON, tool names, schemas, or handler results.

Work starts from `origin/main` (`afb18b0`). Publish as a linear GitHub stack with `gh stack`. Never push `main`. Never touch the dirty `/root/hevy-mcp` checkout.

## Captured requirements

- Keep public `execute()` as Promise; Effect stays internal.
- Collapse operations nested `runPromise` (today: ops `runPromise` → `tryPromise(client.getX())` → client `runPromise(createRequestEffect)`).
- Expose/use internal `createNativeClient.requestEffect` (or equivalent curated internal export). Do **not** add `requestEffect` to the public `HevyClient` type.
- Wire `createCoreServiceLayer` for **all 22** tools (not only the 4 operations-backed ones).
- 18 client tools use `HevyClientService`; 4 ops tools use `HevyOperationsService`; catalog/observer via layer where applicable.
- `ToolRuntime` getters may coexist during migration.
- MCP JSON, 22 names/order, descriptions, annotations, Zod inputs, read `outputSchema`s, and `callTool` results stay unchanged.
- Do not register `get-user-info` (defined but not in the 22).
- Topology-true packages; one Effect runtime boundary at each public Promise API.
- Fresh worktree from `origin/main`; `gh stack` for PRs; never push `main`.
- Mocked unit/PR validation only; no `HEVY_API_KEY`; no live Hevy.

## Expected Functionality

### Milestone 1 — Characterize ops + client Effect seam

Testable, no production behavior change except a curated internal export if tests require it.

- Characterize the four operations Promise contracts: success, missing body, canonical GET 404 → soft `{ expected404Outcome }`, first-page/unrelated/mutation 404 reject with identity-preserved error, list page mismatch reject.
- Characterize that public `HevyClient` stays Promise-only.
- Make `requestEffect` a stable **internal** seam operations can import (today it exists on the Kubb client and is used by `request-effect.test.ts`, but it is not a public `HevyClient` method and is not re-exported from the curated package entry).
- Keep existing operations tests green; add characterization tests before any collapse.

### Milestone 2 — Collapse four operations to one Effect / one `runPromise`

- `workouts.get`, `workouts.list`, `routines.get`, `routines.list` compose `requestEffect` (or adapter Effect methods) instead of `Effect.tryPromise` around Promise client calls.
- Public `execute()` remains `Promise<…>` via a **single** `Effect.runPromise` at that boundary.
- `classifyReadError` stays the pure error-channel predicate; soft 404 outcomes unchanged.
- Callers (core tools, tests, CLI if any) still see Promise resolve/reject.
- Cascade changeset if `packages/operations` (and `hevy-client` if the internal export is a package-visible change) changes.

### Milestone 3 — Wire core layer for all 22 tools

- `createHevyMcpServer` / `ToolRuntime` provide `createCoreServiceLayer` (client, operations, catalog, execution; observer via `createToolObserverLayer` where applicable).
- All 22 registered tools obtain Hevy dependencies from the layer (directly or through runtime helpers backed by the layer).
- Operations-backed 4: `get-workouts`, `get-workout`, `get-routines`, `get-routine`.
- Client-backed 18: `get-workout-events`, `create-workout`, `update-workout`, `replace-workout-exercises`, `create-routine`, `update-routine`, `get-exercise-template`, `get-exercise-history`, `create-exercise-template`, `search-exercise-templates`, `get-routine-folder`, `create-routine-folder`, `get-body-measurements`, `get-body-measurement`, `create-body-measurement`, `update-body-measurement`, `get-training-summary`, `search-routines`.
- Getters may remain as a compatibility facade.
- `EXPECTED_TOOL_NAMES` count stays 22; `register.test.ts` and per-tool tests stay the regression net.

## Architecture

```
MCP tools (22)  --Promise execute-->  ToolRuntime
                      |                    |
                      |                    v
                      |            createCoreServiceLayer
                      |              HevyClientService (18 tools)
                      |              HevyOperationsService (4 tools)
                      |              catalog / execution / observer
                      v
operations.execute()  --single runPromise-->  Effect program
                                              classifyReadError
                                              requestEffect (internal)

                                                    v

```

- Public APIs remain Promise (`HevyClient` methods, `operation.execute()`, tool `execute(runtime, args)`).

- Operations never wrap an already-run client Promise in `tryPromise`.
- Layer is the DI graph for tools; it does not change MCP wire format.
- Packages stay topology-true: `hevy-client → operations → core`; adapters do not import one another.

# Validation Contract

Black-box behavioral assertions. Deterministic / mocked only except VAL-CROSS-008 (GitHub PR via gh). Fake API keys. No live Hevy. No browser.

Pass/fail is unambiguous from this document. Do not treat source-grep-only checks as success unless a heading below names that evidence. Collapse Effect to Promise only at MCP tool handlers, MCP resource readers, and CLI command `execute`.

## Area: Client Seam

Internal `HevyRequestEffectClient` completeness plus public Promise `HevyClient` stability. Domain 404 policy, mutation quirks (except Promise `createRoutine` empty-body), Stream/DateTime, Cache, MCP/CLI collapse, and package-boundary CI live in later areas.

### VAL-CLIENT-001: Public HevyClient stays Promise-shaped at runtime and in types

`createHevyClient(...)` returns an object whose 22 public methods (`getWorkouts`, `getWorkout`, `createWorkout`, `updateWorkout`, `getWorkoutCount`, `getWorkoutEvents`, `getRoutines`, `getRoutineById`, `createRoutine`, `updateRoutine`, `getExerciseTemplates`, `getExerciseTemplate`, `getExerciseHistory`, `createExerciseTemplate`, `getRoutineFolders`, `getRoutineFolder`, `createRoutineFolder`, `getBodyMeasurements`, `getBodyMeasurement`, `createBodyMeasurement`, `updateBodyMeasurement`, `getUserInfo`) each return a thenable `Promise` when invoked. Exported `HevyClient` types every method as `Promise<...>`. Fail if any public method returns an Effect (`_op` / `pipe` / not a thenable), if `"requestEffect" in client` is true, if `client.requestEffect` is defined, if any method is typed as `Effect.Effect<...>`, or if `const _: Promise<unknown> = client.<method>(...)` fails for any public method.

Tool: vitest
Evidence: terminal output of `packages/hevy-client/src/internal-request-effect.test.ts` and `packages/hevy-client` `check:types`

### VAL-CLIENT-002: Main / types / schemas exports do not leak the Effect client or internal symbols

`import * as pub from "@hevy-mcp/hevy-client"` must not contain `requestEffect`, `createRequestEffect`, `getNativeRequestEffect`, `getRequestEffectClient`, `NATIVE_REQUEST_EFFECT`, `HevyRequestEffectClient`, or `NativeRequestEffect`. `import * as types from "@hevy-mcp/hevy-client/types"` and `import * as schemas from "@hevy-mcp/hevy-client/schemas"` must not export any Effect type, Effect client factory, or `Effect.Effect` value. Fail if any of those names exist on the public export objects, or if `types.ts` / `schemas.ts` import `effect`.

Tool: vitest
Evidence: terminal output of `tests/unit/hevy-client-internal-export.test.ts` and `packages/hevy-client/src/internal-request-effect.test.ts`

### VAL-CLIENT-003: `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client/internal` still exports the Effect seam factories and types

`package.json` `exports` continues to expose `"./internal"` → `./src/internal.ts`. `import { getRequestEffectClient, getNativeRequestEffect, createRequestEffect, NATIVE_REQUEST_EFFECT, type HevyRequestEffectClient, type NativeRequestEffect } from "@hevy-mcp/hevy-client/internal"` succeeds. Fail if the subpath is renamed, dropped, or merged into `"."` / `"./types"` / `"./schemas"`.

Tool: vitest
Evidence: terminal output of `tests/unit/hevy-client-internal-export.test.ts`

### VAL-CLIENT-004: NATIVE_REQUEST_EFFECT is a hidden attachment recoverable via getNativeRequestEffect

`createHevyClient` attaches the native interpreter via the non-enumerable `NATIVE_REQUEST_EFFECT` symbol. `"requestEffect" in client` is false; `Object.keys(client)` / enumerable property names do not include the symbol or `"requestEffect"`; `getNativeRequestEffect(client)` returns the same interpreter used by Promise methods. Fail if the seam is a public enumerable field, if it is missing, or if `getNativeRequestEffect` cannot recover it from a curated Promise client.

Tool: vitest
Evidence: terminal output of `packages/hevy-client/src/internal-request-effect.test.ts`

### VAL-CLIENT-005: getNativeRequestEffect throws TypeError on clients without the seam

Calling `getNativeRequestEffect({})` (or any object lacking `requestEffect` / `NATIVE_REQUEST_EFFECT`) throws `TypeError` with message matching `/Expected a Hevy client with the internal request Effect seam/`. Fail if it returns a function, swallows the miss, or throws a generic `Error`.

Tool: vitest
Evidence: terminal output of `packages/hevy-client/src/internal-request-effect.test.ts`

### VAL-CLIENT-006: Effect client exposes exactly the 22 Promise methods, each Effect-valued

`getRequestEffectClient(client)` exposes exactly these 22 methods and no extras that are not on Promise `HevyClient`: `getWorkouts`, `getWorkout`, `createWorkout`, `updateWorkout`, `getWorkoutEvents`, `getWorkoutCount`, `getRoutines`, `getRoutineById`, `createRoutine`, `updateRoutine`, `getExerciseTemplates`, `getExerciseTemplate`, `getExerciseHistory`, `createExerciseTemplate`, `getRoutineFolders`, `getRoutineFolder`, `createRoutineFolder`, `getBodyMeasurements`, `getBodyMeasurement`, `createBodyMeasurement`, `updateBodyMeasurement`, `getUserInfo`. For every method, the value before `Effect.runPromise` is not a `Promise` (`instanceof Promise` is false) and is runnable with `Effect.runPromise`. Fail if any required method is absent, if extras appear, or if any method is `async` / returns a thenable.

Tool: vitest
Evidence: terminal output of `packages/hevy-client/src/internal-request-effect.test.ts`

### VAL-CLIENT-007: Effect vs Promise HTTP matrix matches for all 22 methods

For mocked 200/201 JSON, `Effect.runPromise(effectMethod(...))` equals the Promise twin’s result, and intercepted fetch method/URL/path keys/query/JSON body match. Fail if any row is missing, uses a Promise hop, hits the wrong path, or diverges in payload.

| `getWorkouts` | GET | `/v1/workouts` | — | `page`, `pageSize` | — |
| `getWorkout` | GET | `/v1/workouts/{workoutId}` | `workoutId` | — | — |
| `createWorkout` | POST | `/v1/workouts` | — | — | JSON workout |
| `updateWorkout` | PUT | `/v1/workouts/{workoutId}` | `workoutId` | — | JSON workout |

### VAL-CLIENT-008: Promise createRoutine empty JSON {} → undefined; Effect returns native payload and does not call Promise method

Promise `HevyClient.createRoutine` continues to map an empty JSON object response `{}` to `undefined`. Effect `createRoutine` still POSTs `/v1/routines` as a native Effect; a mocked `{}` body succeeds with that native empty object (or the documented interpreter payload), not `undefined`. Fail if Promise `createRoutine` no longer returns `undefined` for `{}`, if Effect maps `{}` to `undefined`, or if Effect create is implemented by calling the Promise method.

Tool: vitest
Evidence: terminal output of `packages/hevy-client/src/hevy-client.test.ts` and `packages/hevy-client/src/internal-request-effect.test.ts`

### VAL-CLIENT-009: Shared client config: custom fetch, apiKey, maxGetRetries apply equally to Effect methods

`createHevyClient({ fetch, apiKey, maxGetRetries, … })` is what Effect methods use. A custom `fetch`, `maxGetRetries: 0` (or `2`), and fake `apiKey` (`"test-key"`) change Effect attempt count and the `api-key` header the same way they change Promise. Fail if Effect ignores constructor `fetch`, uses a different retry budget, or sends a different `api-key` than Promise for the same client.

Tool: vitest
Evidence: terminal output of `packages/hevy-client/src/internal-request-effect.test.ts`

### VAL-CLIENT-010: GET retry-then-success parity (include existing read AND one new GET: events, count, or list)

With `maxGetRetries: 1` and mocked `503` then `200`, Promise and Effect each fetch twice then succeed with the same payload. Coverage must include at least one existing read (`getWorkout` / `getWorkouts` / `getRoutines` / `getRoutineById`) **and** one new GET added this mission (`getWorkoutEvents`, `getWorkoutCount`, or a new list such as `getExerciseTemplates` / `getRoutineFolders` / `getBodyMeasurements`). Fail if Effect skips retry, retries a different number of times, or succeeds without the second fetch on either sample.

Tool: vitest
Evidence: terminal output of `packages/hevy-client/src/internal-request-effect.test.ts`

### VAL-CLIENT-011: GET retry exhaustion: same attempt count as Promise then failure

With `maxGetRetries: 1` and every fetch `503`, Promise and Effect GET methods each attempt twice and fail. Cover the same existing-plus-new GET pairing as VAL-CLIENT-010. Fail if Effect attempt count differs from Promise.

Tool: vitest
Evidence: terminal output of `packages/hevy-client/src/internal-request-effect.test.ts`

### VAL-CLIENT-012: POST mutations fetch once on 503; PUT attempt count matches Promise

Mocked `503` on POST (`createWorkout` / `createRoutine` / `createExerciseTemplate` / `createRoutineFolder` / `createBodyMeasurement`) results in a single fetch for both Promise and Effect. PUT (`updateWorkout` / `updateRoutine` / `updateBodyMeasurement`) attempt count equals Promise under the same 503 + `maxGetRetries`. Fail if Effect POST retries, if Promise POST starts retrying, or if Effect PUT retries when Promise does not (or vice versa).

Tool: vitest
Evidence: terminal output of `packages/hevy-client/src/internal-request-effect.test.ts`

### VAL-CLIENT-013: 400 and 404 are a single fetch on both surfaces

Mocked 404 and mocked 400 each produce exactly one `fetch` call on both Promise and Effect (no retry of client errors), including GET and write methods. Fail if tagged-error tests pass on the last of N identical 404/400 responses while the interpreter still retries.

Tool: vitest
Evidence: terminal output of `packages/hevy-client/src/internal-request-effect.test.ts`

### VAL-CLIENT-014: HevyRequestOptions accepted on every Effect method; abort/deadline fail like Promise

Every Effect method accepts trailing `HevyRequestOptions` (`signal?`, `deadline?`, `timeoutMs?`). Passing `{ signal }` (already aborted) or `{ timeoutMs: 1 }` / `{ deadline: Date.now() - 1 }` fails with the same abort/deadline outcome family as the Promise method (`HEVY_REQUEST_ABORTED` / `HEVY_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED` or the tagged `NetworkError` projection of those). Fail if new methods omit `options`, if options are accepted but not forwarded, or if Effect ignores abort/deadline/timeout.

Tool: vitest
Evidence: terminal output of `packages/hevy-client/src/internal-request-effect.test.ts` and `packages/hevy-client/src/request-effect.test.ts`

### VAL-CLIENT-015: Effect GET retry delays controllable with TestClock.layer()

Default-client backoff for an Effect GET still advances under `TestClock.layer()` from `effect/testing`: first 503, clock adjust, second 200, with no wall-clock `sleep`. Fail if Effect methods reintroduce Promise `sleep` that ignores `TestClock`.

Tool: vitest
Evidence: terminal output of `packages/hevy-client/src/request-effect.test.ts`

### VAL-CLIENT-016: Effect 404 → NotFoundError

A mocked 404 on Effect `getWorkout`, `getRoutineById`, `getExerciseTemplate`, `getRoutineFolder`, `getBodyMeasurement`, and `getUserInfo` fails the Effect with `NotFoundError` (`_tag === "NotFoundError"`, `status === 404`, `method === "GET"`, canonical `endpoint`, `expected` boolean present). Fail if the failure is a plain `Error`, a raw `HevyHttpError` without tagged projection, or `throw new Error(...)`.

Tool: vitest
Evidence: terminal output of `packages/hevy-client/src/internal-request-effect.test.ts`

### VAL-CLIENT-017: Effect 400 → ValidationError

A mocked 400 on Effect reads and writes (`createWorkout`, `createRoutine`, `createExerciseTemplate`, `updateWorkout`, `getWorkouts`) fails with `ValidationError` (`_tag === "ValidationError"`, `status === 400`, method/endpoint set). Fail if the failure is a generic `Error` or untagged `HevyHttpError`.

Tool: vitest
Evidence: terminal output of `packages/hevy-client/src/internal-request-effect.test.ts`

### VAL-CLIENT-018: Effect 429 → RateLimitError with attempt count matching Promise

A mocked 429 on an Effect method fails with `RateLimitError` (`_tag === "RateLimitError"`, `status === 429`, method/endpoint set; `retryAfterSeconds` populated when `Retry-After` is a numeric-seconds header). Fetch attempt count matches the Promise twin under the same 429 + `maxGetRetries`. Fail if 429 becomes generic `Error`, untagged `HevyHttpError`, or `ApiError`, or if attempt count diverges from Promise.

Tool: vitest
Evidence: terminal output of `packages/hevy-client/src/internal-request-effect.test.ts`

### VAL-CLIENT-019: Other HTTP (401/403/409/500) → ApiError

A mocked 401, 403, 409, or 500 on an Effect method that is not 400/404/429 fails with `ApiError` (`_tag === "ApiError"`, `status` matches, method/endpoint set). Fail if 401 is `NetworkError` or generic `Error`, or if 500/403/409 become `ValidationError` / `NotFoundError` / `RateLimitError`.

Tool: vitest
Evidence: terminal output of `packages/hevy-client/src/internal-request-effect.test.ts`

### VAL-CLIENT-020: Transport/fetch rejection → NetworkError

A mocked `fetch` rejection (`TypeError("fetch failed")`, `ECONNRESET`, timeout) on an Effect method fails with `NetworkError` (`_tag === "NetworkError"`, `retryExhausted` boolean present). Fail if the failure is `new Error(String(cause))` or an untagged exception.

Tool: vitest
Evidence: terminal output of `packages/hevy-client/src/internal-request-effect.test.ts`

### VAL-CLIENT-021: Effect failures are catchTag-discriminated tagged errors

`Effect.catchTag` / `runPromiseExit` on 404/400/429/500/network failures discriminates `NotFoundError | ValidationError | RateLimitError | ApiError | NetworkError`. `_tag` is not erased. Fail if the error channel is typed only as `Error`, if tagged instances lose `_tag`, or if `catchTag("NotFoundError")` (and the other four tags) cannot select the matching failure.

Tool: vitest
Evidence: terminal output of `packages/hevy-client/src/internal-request-effect.test.ts`

### VAL-CLIENT-022: Public Promise methods still reject HevyHttpError, not tagged Effect errors

Public Promise methods continue to reject with `HevyHttpError` (status/method/canonical endpoint) for HTTP failures. Fail if Promise methods start throwing `NotFoundError` / other tagged errors in a way that breaks existing Promise callers, or if they start throwing generic `Error` instead of `HevyHttpError`.

Tool: vitest
Evidence: terminal output of `packages/hevy-client/src/hevy-client.test.ts` and `packages/hevy-client/src/internal-request-effect.test.ts`

### VAL-CLIENT-023: Encoding parity for path/query/body/api-key

For a representative matrix, Effect vs Promise intercepted requests are deep-equal: query `page` / `pageSize` / `since` / `start_date` / `end_date`; path keys `workoutId` / `routineId` / `exerciseTemplateId` (from `getExerciseTemplate(templateId)`) / `folderId` / `date`; JSON bodies for workout/routine/template/folder/measurement create and update; header `api-key` present using fake `"test-key"` only. Fail if Effect sends `templateId` as the path key, drops query params, stringifies body differently from Promise, or logs a real secret.

Tool: vitest
Evidence: terminal output of `packages/hevy-client/src/internal-request-effect.test.ts`

### VAL-CLIENT-024: Invoking Effect method and Promise twin produces two interpreter fetches

Calling an Effect method and the matching Promise method on the same client issues two intercepted fetches (same URL, independent thenables). Fail if both invocations share one fetch / one thenable, or if Effect is implemented as a Promise hop through the public method.

Tool: vitest
Evidence: terminal output of `packages/hevy-client/src/internal-request-effect.test.ts`

## Area: Operations

`@hevy-mcp/operations` Effect-first domain. In-memory `Effect.succeed` / `Effect.fail` adapters or mocked `fetch`. Tests collapse at the test edge. MCP tool names, Cache, resource URIs, and CLI flags live in later areas.

### VAL-OPS-001: Effect-first HevyOperations shape, effect() programs, Effect.fn names, descriptors and safety

`createOperations(client)` returns `HevyOperations` with `workouts` (`list`, `get`, `create`, `update`, `replaceExercises`, `events`, `count`), `routines` (`list`, `get`, `create`, `update`, `search`), `templates` (`get`, `history`, `create`, `listAll`), `folders` (`get`, `create`, `listAll`), `bodyMeasurements` (`list`, `get`, `create`, `update`), `user` (`get`), `workflows` (`trainingSummary`). Every domain method exposes `effect(input, options?)` that returns an Effect (not a native Promise), is authored with `Effect.fn("operations.<domain>.<op>")` plus a generator (never `const f = () => Effect.gen(...)`), and has `descriptor: { id, safety }` with unique ids. Reads (`list`/`get`/`events`/`count`/`search`/`history`/`listAll`/`trainingSummary`) are `safety: "read"`; creates are non-idempotent writes; `update`/`replaceExercises` are writes. Fail if any key/method/`effect` is missing, if a primary callable returns a Promise, if an `Effect.fn` name mismatches, or if a write is annotated `read`.

Tool: vitest
Evidence: terminal output of `packages/operations/src/hevy-operations.test.ts` and `packages/operations/src/effect-collapse.test.ts`

### VAL-OPS-002: Collapse boundary: domain map/catch/quirks live in effect(); optional execute is a single runPromise; tests collapse at the edge

Normalize, tagged-error recovery, pagination mismatch, mutation quirks, and composite scans execute inside `effect()`, not inside an `async execute` body. If `execute` exists it is a single `Effect.runPromise(this.effect(input, options))` with the same arguments and contains no `catchIf` / `map` / page-normalize / payload-build / `while (` pagination. Domain modules do not `runPromise` around map/catch. Tests obtain values by running `operation.effect(...)` with `Effect.runPromise` / `runPromiseExit` (or the thin `execute` one-liner). Fail if `effect-collapse.test.ts` still requires `execute.toString()` to contain `Effect.runPromise` **and** `Effect.catchIf` together.

Tool: vitest
Evidence: terminal output of `packages/operations/src/effect-collapse.test.ts` and `packages/operations/src/workouts.test.ts`

### VAL-OPS-003: PaginationMismatchError is Schema.TaggedError with requested, received, collection; never throw new Error; never a soft-404 success

When a paginated list that returns `page` receives a different number than `input.page`, the Effect fails with `PaginationMismatchError` (`_tag === "PaginationMismatchError"`, fields `requested`, `received`, `collection` for `workouts` / `routines` / `bodyMeasurements` / `workoutEvents` as applicable). Fail if the error is a plain `Error`/`TypeError`, if list source `throw new Error` for page mismatch, if a mismatch test only matches `error.message` on a generic `Error`, or if mismatch succeeds with `expected404Outcome`.

Tool: vitest

Expected 404 recovery is collection-scoped. Writes are never soft-success. Sibling/unrelated 404s are never recovered. Abort is never converted into soft-404 (see VAL-OPS-008). Pass only if every row holds.

     ```bash
     mise exec -- pnpm run check:changeset
     ```
     `test:pr` is exclusive — do not overlap with other heavy lanes.
5. For `open-github-pr`:
   ```bash
   git -C /root/hevy-mcp-effect-ops-layer status --short --branch

   gh pr create --repo chrisdoc/hevy-mcp --base main --head feat/effect-ops-layer --title "feat: Effect-first Hevy operations layer" --body "..."
   ```

**Off-limits:**

- `/root/hevy-mcp` source and its staged changeset
- Existing unrelated worktrees (`hevy-mcp-combined`, `hevy-mcp-effect-*` except this mission’s `hevy-mcp-effect-ops-layer`)
- `packages/hevy-client/src/generated/` (do not hand-edit)
- Rewriting `packages/node` stdio/HTTP/telemetry or `packages/worker` HTTP/OAuth into Effect
- Exporting Effect types from `hevy-mcp` or `@chrisdoc/hevy-cli`
- `git push` to `main`; `--no-verify`; Git in tests; creating Git identities
- Watch-mode Vitest / leftover processes

If you cannot complete work within these boundaries, return to the orchestrator. Never violate them.

## Mission Directives

**Tools:**

- `mise exec --` for all node/pnpm/npx
- Vitest via named lanes / scoped files, never raw undocumented selectors copied into docs
- `gh` only for the final PR feature (`open-github-pr`)
- GitHub MCP is allowed for PR create if `gh` cannot; prefer `gh`

**Skills:** Follow the worker skill named in the feature (`effect-client-worker`, `operations-worker`, `core-runtime-worker`, `cli-worker`). Read `architecture.md`, `validation-contract.md`, and `library/` before coding.

**Dependencies (binding):**

- `effect@^4.0.0-rc.112` (already in hevy-client, operations, core, cli)
- Effect 4 APIs: `Effect.fn`, `Stream.paginate` (not `paginateEffect`), `Cache.make` (not `cachedWithTTL`), `DateTime.now` as an Effect **value**, `Schema.TaggedError`, `Context.Service`, `Layer.succeed`, `TestClock` from `effect/testing`
- Import `Schema` from `effect`, not `@effect/schema`
- Import `effect` from a workspace package that depends on it, never from the repo root

**Other rules:**

- TDD: failing tests first, then implementation
- Conventional Commits (`feat:`, `fix:`, `refactor:`, `test:`, `docs:`, `chore:`)
- Git hooks stay enabled; fix hook failures
- Before every commit that touches `packages/*`: a non-empty Changeset covering the topology cascade (see `library/topology.md`)
- One Effect→Promise collapse per user invocation (MCP tool handler, resource reader, CLI command). Operations Effect programs do not `runPromise` around map/catch
- Fake API keys only
- After source changes: scoped Vitest (file-scoped first, then package/unit) + `mise exec -- pnpm --filter <pkg> run check:types`. Do not leave stale `[VAL-OPS-NNN]` prefixes on tests that no longer match the contract ID.
- Do not run full `test:pr` until the `cli-hygiene` hygiene/PR features
- Do not run two full `test:unit` lanes in parallel

## Worktree

First feature (if the worktree does not exist):

```bash
git fetch origin main
git worktree add -b feat/effect-ops-layer /root/hevy-mcp-effect-ops-layer origin/main
cd /root/hevy-mcp-effect-ops-layer
mise install
mise exec -- pnpm install
mise exec hk -- hk install --mise
```

All later features: `cd /root/hevy-mcp-effect-ops-layer` and commit there. `EndFeatureRun` `repoPath` must be `/root/hevy-mcp-effect-ops-layer`.

## Architecture reminders

- `hevy-client → operations → core`. CLI may import operations. Node/Worker must not import operations or `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client/internal`. Core must not import `/internal`.
- Public `HevyClient` stays Promise. Effect client lives on `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client/internal`.
- Effect Cache is constructed **once** in `createHevyMcpServer`, then `Layer.succeed` into request-local DI.
- Mutation quirks belong in operations, shared by tools and CLI.

## Testing & Validation Guidance

Validators: deterministic only. No agent-browser. No live Hevy.

**Milestone gate (scrutiny):** `commands.typecheck` = `mise exec -- pnpm run check:types`; `commands.test` = `mise exec -- pnpm run test:unit`. Full `check` + `test:pr` is last-milestone worker work (`release-hygiene-and-changeset`), not every scrutiny run.

**User-testing surfaces:** MCP tool/resource Vitest (`packages/core/src/tools/*.test.ts`, `packages/core/src/resources/hevy.test.ts`) and CLI (`mise exec -- pnpm run test:cli`). Max 2 concurrent validators; prefer 1 if the host is busy. Last-milestone `test:pr` is exclusive.

**Credentials:** none. Fixtures: `packages/core/test-fixtures/mock-hevy.ts`, operations in-memory `Effect.succeed`/`fail`, `packages/cli/src/test-fixtures/effect-client.ts`.

**Skip:** live lanes (`test:live`, `test:integration`, `test:worker-http:live`, `test:nightly`), `inspect`, browser.

See `library/user-testing.md`.

# Single source of truth for commands. No long-running services.
# Milestone scrutiny gate (user-confirmed): typecheck + unit only.
# Full check + test:pr is last-milestone worker work, not every scrutiny run.

commands:
  install: mise exec -- pnpm install
  typecheck: mise exec -- pnpm run check:types
  test: mise exec -- pnpm run test:unit
  lint: "true"
  build: mise exec -- pnpm run build
  check: mise exec -- pnpm run check
  boundaries: mise exec -- pnpm run check:boundaries
  changeset: mise exec -- pnpm run check:changeset
  test-pr: mise exec -- pnpm run test:pr
  test-cli: mise exec -- pnpm run test:cli
  test-performance: mise exec -- pnpm run test:performance

### VAL-CORE-027: No leftover client RMW, payload builders, or workflow loops in tools

After wiring: `packages/core/src/tools/workouts.ts` does not call `buildWorkoutUpdatePayload` or `client.getWorkout` + `client.updateWorkout`. `packages/core/src/tools/routines.ts` does not call `buildRoutinePayload`. `packages/core/src/tools/body-measurements.ts` does not call `buildMeasurementPayload`. `packages/core/src/tools/workflows.ts` does not contain `scanPagesInWindow`, `getPeriod`, `Promise.all`, or UTC `Date` arithmetic. `packages/core/src/tools/routine-discovery.ts` does not contain `discoverRoutines` pagination. Tools remain taxonomy + schema + `respond`. Quirk correctness is VAL-OPS-033–036.

Tool: vitest
Evidence: terminal output of `packages/core/src/tools/workouts.test.ts`, `packages/core/src/tools/routines.test.ts`, `packages/core/src/tools/body-measurements.test.ts`, `packages/core/src/tools/workflows.test.ts`, `packages/core/src/tools/routine-discovery.test.ts`

### VAL-CORE-028: First callTool uses the layer-backed operations instance

When `runtime.getOperations()` is spied to return a divergent object, the first `callTool` still uses `HevyOperationsService` from the request layer (expanded to every registered tool). Tools keep operations on the parent layer and pass `runtime.execution` into the Effect program rather than rebinding via `HevyClientService` on `forExecution`.

Tool: vitest
Evidence: terminal output of `packages/core/src/tools/cross-package.test.ts`

## Area: CLI

Lane: `pnpm run test:cli`. Fake API keys only. No live Hevy.

### VAL-CLI-001: hevy --help / --version work without credentials or Effect

`hevy --help` and `hevy --version` (and `-h` / `-v`) still exit 0 without reading `HEVY_API_KEY`, without constructing a `HevyClient`, and without collapsing an Effect. Help text still lists the public command families (`user`, `workouts`, `routines`, `exercises`, `measurements`, `folders`, `summary`). Version still prints to stdout; stderr stays empty.

Tool: vitest (`pnpm run test:cli`)
Evidence: terminal output of `packages/cli/src/main.test.ts`

### VAL-CLI-002: workouts list stays on operations.workouts.list

`hevy workouts list` continues to call `operations.workouts.list` (Effect program, collapsed once in the command handler). It must not call `client.getWorkouts` directly. Page envelope, `--page` / `--page-size`, and `expected404Outcome: "end_of_list"` → empty page envelope remain compatible with the current CLI stdout contract.

Tool: vitest (`pnpm run test:cli`)
Evidence: terminal output of `packages/cli/src/commands/index.test.ts`

### VAL-CLI-003: routines list stays on operations.routines.list

`hevy routines list` continues to call `operations.routines.list` (Effect program, collapsed once in the command handler). It must not call `client.getRoutines` directly. Page envelope, pagination flags, and end-of-list 404 mapping stay compatible.

Tool: vitest (`pnpm run test:cli`)
Evidence: terminal output of `packages/cli/src/commands/index.test.ts`

### VAL-CLI-004: Remaining domain commands use operations, not HevyClient

Every remaining CLI domain command obtains data through `HevyOperations`, not ad-hoc `HevyClient` methods. Injected operations stubs (or Effect adapters from `packages/cli/src/test-fixtures/effect-client.ts`) are invoked and the matching `client.*` method is **not** called. CLI argument parsing, confirmation (`--yes`), and `--data` loading stay in the CLI. Domain policy (404, pagination, mutation quirks, date windows) lives in operations.

| Command | Operation |
|---|---|
| `hevy user` | `operations.user.get` |
| `hevy workouts get <id>` | `operations.workouts.get` |
| `hevy workouts create --data … --yes` | `operations.workouts.create` |
| `hevy workouts update <id> --data … --yes` | `operations.workouts.update` |
| `hevy workouts count` | `operations.workouts.count` |
| `hevy workouts events` | `operations.workouts.events` |
| `hevy routines get <id>` | `operations.routines.get` |
| `hevy routines create --data … --yes` | `operations.routines.create` |
| `hevy routines update <id> --data … --yes` | `operations.routines.update` |
| `hevy exercises create --data … --yes` | `operations.templates.create` |
| `hevy exercises get <id>` | `operations.templates.get` |
| `hevy exercises history <id>` | `operations.templates.history` |
| `hevy exercises search <query>` | operations composite (templates catalog / search), not a local `while` + `client.getExerciseTemplates` loop |
| `hevy measurements list` | `operations.bodyMeasurements.list` |
| `hevy measurements get <date>` | `operations.bodyMeasurements.get` |
| `hevy measurements create <date> --data … --yes` | `operations.bodyMeasurements.create` |
| `hevy measurements update <date> --data … --yes` | `operations.bodyMeasurements.update` |
| `hevy folders create --data … --yes` | `operations.folders.create` |
| `hevy summary` | `operations.workflows.trainingSummary`, not `collectSummaryWorkouts` over `client.getWorkouts` |

Tool: vitest (`pnpm run test:cli`)
Evidence: terminal output of `packages/cli/src/commands/index.test.ts`

### VAL-CLI-005: Effect collapses once per CLI command handler

Each CLI command `execute` path performs exactly one `Effect.runPromise` / `runPromiseExit` (or the documented handler-edge equivalent) for that user invocation. Command handlers may call `operation.effect(...)` and collapse at the handler. They must not call nested `runPromise` inside argument mapping, pagination loops, or stdout formatting. If `operation.execute` still exists, it is a trivial `Effect.runPromise(this.effect(...))` adapter and is **not** used as a second collapse on top of a handler `runPromise`.

Tool: vitest (`pnpm run test:cli`)
Evidence: terminal output of `packages/cli/src/commands/index.test.ts`

### VAL-CLI-006: @chrisdoc/hevy-cli does not export Effect types

The public CLI package remains a bin-only Promise-shaped surface (`hevy` → `dist/cli.mjs`). It must not add a public `exports` map that re-exports `Effect`, `HevyOperations` Effect programs, or `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client/internal`; must not publish `.d.ts` entry points that mention `effect` types; must not document or type-export Effect as part of the package API. `effect` may be a CLI workspace dependency used internally. Consumers of `@chrisdoc/hevy-cli` only get the `hevy` binary.

Tool: vitest (`pnpm run test:cli`)
Evidence: terminal output of CLI package-export inspection in the CLI lane

### VAL-CLI-007: CLI flags, stdout/stderr, exit codes stay compatible

`--json` still writes machine-readable JSON to stdout on success and JSON diagnostics to stderr on failure. Human mode still writes the existing human/JSON-envelope result to stdout and concise messages to stderr. `--page`, `--page-size`, `--since`, `--start-date`, `--end-date`, `--max-pages`, `--weeks`, `--data`, `--yes` keep the same names, parsing, and usage errors (e.g. `--page must be a positive integer` on stderr, exit 2, no `ZodError` leak). Mutations still require `--yes`; missing `--data` is still a usage error. Missing `HEVY_API_KEY` still exits non-zero with a stderr message that mentions `HEVY_API_KEY` and writes nothing to stdout. API/pagination failures still classify as API failures (`ApiResponseError`), not untyped defects. No real API keys appear in argv, logs, fixtures, or error text (fake keys only).

Tool: vitest (`pnpm run test:cli`)
Evidence: terminal output of `packages/cli/src/main.test.ts`, `packages/cli/src/arguments.test.ts`, `packages/cli/src/commands/index.test.ts`

### VAL-CLI-008: CLI may import operations; must not import node, worker, or hevy-client/internal

`packages/cli` may import `@hevy-mcp/operations`, `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client` (`""` / `schemas`), `@hevy-mcp/core` (`""` / `mutations`), and `effect` internally. It must not import `hevy-mcp` / `packages/node`, `@hevy-mcp/worker` / `packages/worker`, or `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client/internal`. Source and test files under `packages/cli` have no such import.

Tool: vitest (`pnpm run test:cli`)
Evidence: terminal output of CLI package tests / static import assertion

### VAL-CLI-009: Command execution options (abort/deadline) forward into operation.effect

CLI command handlers forward abort/deadline execution options into `operation.effect` (one collapse at the handler). Fail if a command invokes operations without the execution bag, or if abort/deadline is applied only to a leftover Promise `HevyClient` call. Do not re-test the HTTP interpreter (VAL-CLIENT-014) or domain catch (VAL-OPS-008).

Tool: vitest (`pnpm run test:cli`)
Evidence: terminal output of `packages/cli/src/commands/index.test.ts`

## Cross-Area Flows

Flows that span packages. Deterministic except VAL-CROSS-008.

### VAL-CROSS-001: MCP tools and CLI share one operations implementation for mutations

A representative mutation quirk — create/update routine `rep_range` (fixed-rep promotion, `usesRepRanges` / wire payload) — is implemented once in `@hevy-mcp/operations` and consumed by both MCP tools (`packages/core/src/tools/routines.ts` via `HevyOperationsService`) and CLI (`hevy routines create` / `hevy routines update`). Core `mutation-semantics.ts` / `hevy-quirks.ts` are no longer a second source of truth. Feeding the same routine input through the tool handler and the CLI command produces the same operations call. Neither path calls `HevyClient.createRoutine` / `updateRoutine` directly. Payload-byte correctness is VAL-OPS-035.
